claim: Stem: "Which legendary player RETURNED FROM EXILE to play for Napoli in the 1980s?" Maradona was never in exile; he transferred to Napoli from Barcelona in July 1984 for a then world-record fee. The "exile" clause is an invented biographical premise.
q: Which legendary player returned from exile to play for Napoli in the 1980s and transformed the club?

claim: Stem names the "Battle of SANTIAGO" in 1962, and "Chile vs Italy" is the only option containing Chile. Anyone who knows Santiago is Chile's capital — no football knowledge required — picks it by elimination.
q: The 'Battle of Santiago' in 1962 saw two players sent off and police on the pitch — between which nations?

claim: Stem says the record was set "under ROBERTO MANCINI" and the options are Brazil, France, Spain, Italy. Recognising an Italian name — not football knowledge — is enough to answer.
q: Which nation holds the world record for the longest unbeaten run in international football — 37 games, under Roberto Mancini?

claim: Stem says Man Utd won the first Premier League title "with a record 84 points". 84 was not a record in the English top flight: under three-points-for-a-win, Liverpool (1987-88) and Everton (1984-85) both finished on 90 points, and Arsenal had 83 in 1990-91 after a 2-point deduction. Being the first PL season, any total was trivially a 'PL record' — but as written the stem asserts a points record that is false.
q: Which club won the first ever Premier League title with a record 84 points?

claim: Stem says Mourinho "famously said his team would 'park the bus'". He said the opposite: after Chelsea 0-0 Tottenham in Sept 2004 he complained that TOTTENHAM "brought the bus and left the bus in front of the goal". The phrase was a criticism of the opponent, not a description of his own side. The keyed answer (Mourinho) is right, but the stem reverses the meaning of the quote.
q: Which manager famously said his team would 'park the bus' — now a common football phrase?

claim: Stem claims Immobile "holds the record for most Serie A Capocannoniere wins as a Lazio player — three times". Giuseppe Signori also won three Capocannoniere titles as a Lazio player (1992-93, 1993-94, 1995-96), so the record is shared, not held. Immobile's three (2017-18, 2019-20, 2021-22) is correct as a count; the exclusivity claim is not.
q: Which Italian striker holds the record for most Serie A Capocannoniere (top scorer) wins as a Lazio player — three times?
